prompt:
You are judging a short video clip (sampled frames shown in order) for a highlight-reel agent.

Moment types (the rubric):
- made_basket: A player on either team makes a two-point basket. Require visible made outcome; exclude misses and free throws.
- three_pointer: A player on either team makes a shot from beyond the three-point arc; require visible made outcome and clear shooting position.
- layup_or_dunk: A player on either team completes a made layup or dunk; require the made outcome.
- steal: Either team clearly takes the ball from the opponent through an interception or strip and establishes control.
- rebound: After a visibly missed shot, a player on either team clearly secures control of the ball. Identify the team.
- block: A defender on either team visibly contacts and deflects an attempted shot.

Who/what to look for: Highlights from BOTH teams: light-blue and black jerseys. Identify which team makes each play in your reason. Include only clearly completed basketball events.
Set subject_present=true only when the subject described above is the one making the play in the foreground game; false otherwise.

Rejection rules (apply these first):
- Judge ONLY the primary game in the foreground — the court with the referees and the two teams playing in formation. IGNORE any action on adjacent or background courts and anyone shooting on a side basket.
- Return moment_type=null (low confidence) if the frames show a timeout, huddle, or players standing around during a dead ball; warm-ups or shoot-around; substitutions or walking to the bench; or a camera pan/zoom with motion blur and no clear play.
- When you are not confident a real play from the rubric is happening, return null rather than guessing — a padded reel is worse than a short one.
- Never include: timeouts, bench_sequences, shaky_camera, dead_ball_standing_around, warm_ups.
- Grounding rule: Only label visually supported completed events. Do not invent an outcome or a player identity.

Look at the frames and decide whether this window contains one of the moment types above and whether the subject is visible.

Basketball temporal checks:
- The first and last images provide before/after context. The middle images densely sample the candidate action. Classify the central action; do not label an unrelated event visible only in the outer context.
- Treat the images as an ordered sequence, not independent pictures. Compare who controls the ball in the first and last frames.
- A steal requires visible evidence that the defending team gains or deflects possession; a rebound after a shot is not a steal.
- Only select event types explicitly listed in this recipe. Rebounds are allowed when the rubric includes them; do not substitute a steal or basket for a rebound.
- Do not call a rebound a steal merely because possession changes teams. A steal requires a defender disrupting a live dribble or pass before control.
- A made basket requires visible outcome evidence (ball through the rim/net or unmistakable immediate aftermath). A ball in the air is only an attempt.
- A three_pointer additionally requires clear evidence that the shooter was behind the three-point line. If distance or make is unclear, do not guess.
- Prefer null when the ordered frames do not establish the complete event.

Respond with STRICT JSON only, no prose, no markdown fences, matching exactly this shape:
{"moment_type": <string or null>, "subject_present": <true|false>, "confidence": <number 0..1>, "reason": <short string>}
You are receiving continuous video, not sparse still images. Clip00:00 is source421.0s. The candidate action interval is [426.5,427.5] source seconds. Use surrounding video to verify the complete action. Classify the central action, not every frame. For rebounds determine shooting and controlling teams; a rebound is permitted when present in the rubric.
